concepts.title: Prime factorisation
concepts.explanation: Break a positive integer into prime factors. A perfect square has even prime exponents; a perfect cube has exponents divisible by three.

example.problem: Find the least multiplier that makes 72 a square.
steps: The exponent of 2 is odd. Multiply by 2.

concepts.commonMistake: Adding to the number does not repair prime exponents in its factorisation.
checklist: Multiply or divide as the question requests.

concepts.title: Highest common factor
concepts.explanation: HCF uses only shared prime factors, each with its smaller exponent. It divides both numbers exactly.
concepts.commonMistake: Choosing the larger exponents gives the LCM, not the HCF.
checklist: Check that the result divides both numbers.

concepts.title: Lowest common multiple
concepts.explanation: LCM uses every prime present, each with its largest exponent. It is the first positive time that repeating integer cycles align.

example.problem: Two bells ring every 6 and 8 minutes. When do they next ring together?
steps: They next ring together after 24 minutes.

concepts.commonMistake: The product is a common multiple, but may not be the least common multiple.
checklist: Check divisibility by each given number.

concepts.title: Irrational numbers
concepts.explanation: A rational number is p/q for integers p and q ≠ 0. The square root of a prime is irrational. Rational operations can sometimes cancel an irrational term.

steps: But √3 is irrational. This contradiction proves the claim.

concepts.commonMistake: Two irrational numbers can have a rational product: √3 × √3 = 3.
checklist: In a contradiction proof, start with a fraction in lowest terms.

concepts.title: HCF–LCM relationship
concepts.explanation: For two positive integers a and b, HCF(a,b) × LCM(a,b) = a × b. Check the HCF and LCM as well as the product when verifying a proposed pair.

example.problem: HCF is 6, LCM is 72, and one integer is 18. Find the other.

concepts.commonMistake: The product identity alone does not guarantee that a proposed pair has the required HCF.
checklist: Divide by the known integer when appropriate.

questions.prompt: Which is the prime factorisation of 72?
questions.explanation: 72 = 2³ × 3². Each base is prime.

questions.prompt: Which is the prime factorisation of 108?
questions.explanation: 108 = 2² × 3³. Each base is prime.

questions.prompt: Which is the prime factorisation of 200?
questions.explanation: 200 = 2³ × 5². Each base is prime.

questions.prompt: What is the least positive integer by which 72 must be divided to give a perfect square?
questions.explanation: Remove the prime factor with an odd exponent: 72/2 = 36, a perfect square.

questions.prompt: What is the least positive integer by which 108 must be divided to give a perfect square?
questions.explanation: Remove the prime factor with an odd exponent: 108/3 = 36, a perfect square.

questions.prompt: What is the least positive integer by which 200 must be divided to give a perfect square?
questions.explanation: Remove the prime factor with an odd exponent: 200/2 = 100, a perfect square.

questions.prompt: What is the least positive integer by which 72 must be multiplied to give a perfect cube?
questions.explanation: Complete prime exponents to multiples of three: 72 × 3 = 216, a perfect cube.

questions.prompt: What is the least positive integer by which 108 must be multiplied to give a perfect cube?
questions.explanation: Complete prime exponents to multiples of three: 108 × 2 = 216, a perfect cube.

questions.prompt: What is the least positive integer by which 200 must be multiplied to give a perfect cube?
questions.explanation: Complete prime exponents to multiples of three: 200 × 5 = 1000, a perfect cube.

questions.prompt: Which is the greatest positive integer that divides both 36 and 60?
questions.explanation: HCF(36, 60) = 12. It divides both numbers exactly.

questions.prompt: Which is the greatest positive integer that divides both 54 and 90?
questions.explanation: HCF(54, 90) = 18. It divides both numbers exactly.

questions.prompt: Which is the greatest positive integer that divides both 80 and 120?
questions.explanation: HCF(80, 120) = 40. It divides both numbers exactly.

questions.prompt: Two ribbons measure 84 cm and 144 cm. What is the greatest equal piece length (cm) that leaves no waste?
questions.explanation: The piece length must divide both lengths. HCF(84, 144) = 12 cm.

questions.prompt: Two ribbons measure 96 cm and 160 cm. What is the greatest equal piece length (cm) that leaves no waste?
questions.explanation: The piece length must divide both lengths. HCF(96, 160) = 32 cm.

questions.prompt: Two ribbons measure 105 cm and 175 cm. What is the greatest equal piece length (cm) that leaves no waste?
questions.explanation: The piece length must divide both lengths. HCF(105, 175) = 35 cm.

questions.prompt: A teacher has 96 pencils and 144 erasers. All are split into the greatest possible number of identical packs. How many packs can be made?
questions.explanation: The number of packs divides both counts: HCF = 48. Each pack has 2 pencils and 3 erasers.

questions.prompt: A teacher has 126 pencils and 180 erasers. All are split into the greatest possible number of identical packs. How many packs can be made?
questions.explanation: The number of packs divides both counts: HCF = 18. Each pack has 7 pencils and 10 erasers.

questions.prompt: A teacher has 168 pencils and 252 erasers. All are split into the greatest possible number of identical packs. How many packs can be made?
questions.explanation: The number of packs divides both counts: HCF = 84. Each pack has 2 pencils and 3 erasers.

questions.prompt: Find the LCM of 8 and 12.
questions.explanation: The least positive multiple of both 8 and 12 is 24.

questions.prompt: Find the LCM of 9 and 15.
questions.explanation: The least positive multiple of both 9 and 15 is 45.

questions.prompt: Find the LCM of 14 and 21.
questions.explanation: The least positive multiple of both 14 and 21 is 42.

questions.prompt: Two bells ring together now and repeat every 12 and 18 minutes. After how many minutes do they next ring together?
questions.explanation: Find the first shared cycle: LCM(12, 18) = 36 minutes.

questions.prompt: Two bells ring together now and repeat every 15 and 20 minutes. After how many minutes do they next ring together?
questions.explanation: Find the first shared cycle: LCM(15, 20) = 60 minutes.

questions.prompt: Two bells ring together now and repeat every 16 and 24 minutes. After how many minutes do they next ring together?
questions.explanation: Find the first shared cycle: LCM(16, 24) = 48 minutes.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest positive integer divisible by each of 8, 12 and 18?
questions.explanation: Use the greatest exponent of every prime in all three factorisations. Their LCM is 72.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest positive integer divisible by each of 6, 15 and 20?
questions.explanation: Use the greatest exponent of every prime in all three factorisations. Their LCM is 60.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest positive integer divisible by each of 9, 12 and 30?
questions.explanation: Use the greatest exponent of every prime in all three factorisations. Their LCM is 180.

questions.prompt: Which number is irrational? (Consider √2.)
questions.explanation: 2 is prime, so √2 is irrational. √81 = 9; the decimal and fraction are rational.

questions.prompt: Which number is irrational? (Consider √3.)
questions.explanation: 3 is prime, so √3 is irrational. √81 = 9; the decimal and fraction are rational.

questions.prompt: Which number is irrational? (Consider √7.)
questions.explanation: 7 is prime, so √7 is irrational. √81 = 9; the decimal and fraction are rational.

questions.prompt: Which expression involving √2 is irrational?
questions.explanation: The other expressions equal 2, 0 and 1. Adding rational 1 to irrational √2 stays irrational.

questions.prompt: Which expression involving √3 is irrational?
questions.explanation: The other expressions equal 3, 0 and 1. Adding rational 1 to irrational √3 stays irrational.

questions.prompt: Which expression involving √7 is irrational?
questions.explanation: The other expressions equal 7, 0 and 1. Adding rational 1 to irrational √7 stays irrational.

questions.prompt: Suppose √2 = a/b in lowest terms. Squaring gives a² = 2b². Which argument completes the contradiction?
options: Both a and b must equal zero.
Squaring a fraction always makes it an integer.
The equation proves 2 is not prime.
Prime 2 divides a, and substitution then shows it divides b, contradicting lowest terms.
questions.explanation: If prime 2 divides a², it divides a. Write a = 2k; substitution gives b² = 2k², so 2 also divides b. This contradicts coprimality.

questions.prompt: Suppose √3 = a/b in lowest terms. Squaring gives a² = 3b². Which argument completes the contradiction?
options: Squaring a fraction always makes it an integer.
The equation proves 3 is not prime.
Prime 3 divides a, and substitution then shows it divides b, contradicting lowest terms.
Both a and b must equal zero.
questions.explanation: If prime 3 divides a², it divides a. Write a = 3k; substitution gives b² = 3k², so 3 also divides b. This contradicts coprimality.

questions.prompt: Suppose √7 = a/b in lowest terms. Squaring gives a² = 7b². Which argument completes the contradiction?
options: The equation proves 7 is not prime.
Prime 7 divides a, and substitution then shows it divides b, contradicting lowest terms.
Both a and b must equal zero.
Squaring a fraction always makes it an integer.
questions.explanation: If prime 7 divides a², it divides a. Write a = 7k; substitution gives b² = 7k², so 7 also divides b. This contradicts coprimality.

questions.prompt: Two positive integers have HCF 12 and LCM 72. One integer is 24. Find the other.
questions.explanation: The other integer is (12 × 72)/24 = 36.

questions.prompt: Two positive integers have HCF 6 and LCM 120. One integer is 30. Find the other.
questions.explanation: The other integer is (6 × 120)/30 = 24.

questions.prompt: Two positive integers have HCF 8 and LCM 120. One integer is 24. Find the other.
questions.explanation: The other integer is (8 × 120)/24 = 40.

questions.prompt: Two positive integers have product 540 and HCF 6. What is their LCM?
questions.explanation: LCM = product/HCF = 540/6 = 90.

questions.prompt: Two positive integers have product 960 and HCF 8. What is their LCM?
questions.explanation: LCM = product/HCF = 960/8 = 120.

questions.prompt: Two positive integers have product 1176 and HCF 14. What is their LCM?
questions.explanation: LCM = product/HCF = 1176/14 = 84.

questions.prompt: Which pair has HCF 6 and LCM 90?
questions.explanation: 18 = 6 × 3, 30 = 6 × 5; 3 and 5 are coprime. Their HCF is 6 and LCM is 90.

questions.prompt: Which pair has HCF 4 and LCM 84?
questions.explanation: 12 = 4 × 3, 28 = 4 × 7; 3 and 7 are coprime. Their HCF is 4 and LCM is 84.

questions.prompt: Which pair has HCF 5 and LCM 180?
questions.explanation: 20 = 5 × 4, 45 = 5 × 9; 4 and 9 are coprime. Their HCF is 5 and LCM is 180.
